name: StockOS – One Stock Count Across Shopify, Amazon & Flipkart: Order Polling, Dedupe, Safety Buffer, Push & Low-Stock Alerts

parameters.content:
# StockOS – One Stock Count Across Shopify, Amazon & Flipkart

For Indian D2C brands selling the same stock on their Shopify store, Amazon and Flipkart, and keeping it in sync with a spreadsheet and a lot of hope. When one channel sells the last unit and the others don't know, you get oversells, cancellations and marketplace penalties.

## How it works
Every 10 minutes the workflow collects new and cancelled orders from all three channels. It deducts each order line from one master count exactly once, using a ledger, then pushes the new sellable quantity (on-hand minus a safety buffer) only to SKUs that changed. A nightly full resync catches anything missed. Low-stock, out-of-stock and oversold SKUs are posted to Slack with days of cover based on recent sales. A simple form lets the warehouse log recounts and new stock.

## Setup steps
1. Create a Google Sheet with **Inventory Master** (SKU, on-hand, buffer, Shopify, Amazon and Flipkart IDs), **Processed Lines**, **Stock Adjustments** and **Sync State** tabs.
2. Connect Shopify (Header Auth with `X-Shopify-Access-Token`), Flipkart (Basic Auth with app ID and secret), Google Sheets and Slack.
3. In **Set Sync Config**, set your store, Amazon seller ID, SP-API (LWA) app details and Flipkart location ID.
4. Run once manually and check the master sheet before activating.

## Schedule & Sync Cursor
Runs every 10 minutes. The last successful sync time is read and pulled back 5 minutes, so an order landing between two runs is never missed. On the very first run it looks back 24 hours.

## Load Inventory & Ledger
Loads the master stock count, the ledger of order lines already counted, and any manual adjustments waiting to be applied. The ledger is what stops the same order being deducted twice.

## Shopify & Amazon Orders
Fetches Shopify orders updated since the cursor, then gets a fresh Amazon SP-API token and lists Amazon orders updated in the same window.

## Amazon Order Items
Amazon's order list has no SKUs, so line items are fetched one order at a time, about one request every two seconds, to stay inside SP-API rate limits. Runs with no Amazon orders skip straight to Flipkart.

## Flipkart Orders
Gets a Flipkart token, then pulls new shipments waiting for dispatch and any recent cancellations, so cancelled units go back into stock.

## Stock Math
The core of the workflow. Each sale is deducted and each cancellation added back exactly once, adjustments are applied, and sellable stock is worked out as on-hand minus the safety buffer.

## Push to Shopify
Only SKUs whose sellable quantity changed are sent, using the inventory set-quantities mutation.

## Push to Amazon
Updates the listing quantity per SKU through the Listings API. Any failed push, from any channel, is posted to Slack with the error.

## Push to Flipkart
Sends changed quantities in batches to your Flipkart location. Once a night every SKU is pushed as a full resync.

## Master & Ledger
Writes the new on-hand and sellable counts back to the master sheet, and records every order line processed in this run.

## Adjustments & Cursor
Marks queued manual adjustments as applied and moves the sync cursor forward for the next run.

## Low-Stock Alerts
Oversold, out-of-stock and low SKUs go to Slack, with days of cover worked out from the last 14 days of sales.

## Manual Stock Adjustments
Warehouse staff log a recount, damage or new stock through the form. It's validated, queued, and applied to all three channels on the next sync.

## Credentials & Security
Shopify and Flipkart keys live in n8n credentials. The Amazon LWA client secret and refresh token sit in the config node, so restrict who can open this workflow and its executions. Give each marketplace app inventory and order scopes only.
